_comment: Device and LED inventory. Indices and names come from SimAppPro's www/js/DeviceConfig.js; part ids come from a broadcast ONLINE_HEARTBEAT. See docs/PROTOCOL.md.
_status: PTO2 and Orion Throttle Base II both fully verified 2026-09-16. Indices 0/1/2 are dimmers taking 0-255. Indices 4-17 are indicators taking 0 or 1 only; a value of 255 is out of range and is silently ignored (it acks, and nothing lights). CarrierAce UFC + HUD verified 2026-09-17: three dimmers and a segment display, no indicators. CarrierAce MFD verified 2026-09-18: one dimmer, under three names and PIDs. Orion Combat Rudder Pedals verified 2026-09-18: three dimmers at 0, 1 and 3; index 2 writes both pedal lights and is left alone.

_evidence.dimmer: Indices 0, 1 and 2 observed taking 1, 2, 11, 13, 20, 22, 111, 137, 200, 222 and 255 from SimAppPro's sliders.
_evidence.indicator: SimAppPro only ever sends 0 or 1 to indices 4..17. Confirmed on hardware: 1 lights, 0 clears, 255 does nothing.
_evidence.hook_dimness: Index 17 (HOOK) is a physically dim lamp - visibly weaker than its neighbours even at full brightness. It is not a protocol difference.

_open_questions: None open. The last one - how the governing dimmers behave - was isolated on hardware 2026-09-16; see the SL and Backlight notes on each device.

leds.name: HOOK
leds.label: HOOK
leds.note: Physically dim lamp; hard to see at distance. Not a protocol quirk.

_notes: Index 3 is the FLAG dimmer, exposed in SimAppPro as the 'flag' slider. It was missing from the vendor table we transcribed, which cost a debugging session: the engine drove the flap lamps correctly and they were invisible because FLAG was parked near 0.

THREE INDEPENDENT BRIGHTNESS GROUPS, not one. Measured 2026-09-16 with every indicator held at 1: SL (2) gates all of 4-17 hard. FLAG (3) governs NOSE, LEFT, RIGHT, FLAPS, HALF, FULL and HOOK beneath it; at FLAG=0 those seven are invisible while CAUTION, JETT, CTR, LI, LO, RO and RI stay lit. Backlight (0) drives the panel labels and governs neither indicator group.
Index 1 carries the vendor's name Landing_gear_lights, but setting it to 0 with all 14 indicators lit changed nothing visible. What it drives is unidentified, so the name is not evidence.
Indicators take 0 or 1. Writing 255 acks and does nothing - it is out of range, not truthy.
The 14 indicators match SimAppPro's UI list read top to bottom, which is how the index order was corroborated.

SL (index 2) is a MASTER GATE for indices 4-17: with SL at 0 no indicator lights at all, whatever value it is sent. Isolated 2026-09-16: SL=0 then CAUTION=1 acked and stayed dark. Stronger than the Orion II, where Backlight only dims.

Indicator values LATCH INDEPENDENTLY of SL. Raising SL from 0 to 255 without rewriting the indicator brought CAUTION up at full brightness on its own. So SL is applied downstream of the latched per-LED value, and a change to SL never requires the engine to re-sweep the indicators - the hardware re-applies them.

One USB interface, three parts, all answering a broadcast heartbeat. usb_pid 48484 (0xbd64) is the composite enumeration for base + these handles and changes if different handles are fitted, so parts are discovered rather than trusted from the PID.
Handle LED inventories are unknown and left empty rather than guessed.
Verified 2026-09-16 on hardware and against a SimAppPro HID capture. Index 0 is a dimmer; indices 1 and 2 are binary indicators - SimAppPro only ever sends 0 or 1 to them.

Index 0 (Backlight) governs the BRIGHTNESS of indices 1 and 2, but does not gate them: with Backlight at 0 the A/A and A/G lamps are still lit, just very dim. Brightness rises with Backlight. So a profile that binds A/A without binding Backlight yields a visible but very dim lamp, not a dead one.

Unlike the PTO2, this device LIGHTS an indicator when sent 255 rather than ignoring the out-of-range value. Brightness is identical at 1, 30 and 255 because the value is binary here and Backlight sets the level. Write 1, which is what the vendor sends.
SimAppPro does not clamp the Backlight field: entering 1255 transmitted 231 (0x4E7 truncated to its low byte 0xE7). That is a SimAppPro defect, not a device range.

leds.name: INST_PNL_Backlight
leds.label: Panel backlight
leds.note: Lights the legends only. The glass has its own dimmer.

leds.name: LCDBacklight
leds.label: LCD backlight
leds.note: Lights the segment display: bound like any lamp, but it lights only while a profile puts fields on the screen and is 0 when nothing is drawn there. Every default holds it at full. At 0 the glass is dark even when the cells are being driven correctly.

leds.name: HUD_INST_PNL_Backlight
leds.label: HUD panel backlight
leds.note: Index 1 on part 0xbe0e, not 0. There is no index 0 on this part as far as SimAppPro is concerned, and it was never addressed in a capture. This looks like a transcription slip and is not. Renamed from the vendor's INST_PNL_Backlight because the UFC part carries a lamp of that name too, and a profile names a lamp by device and name.

_notes: Verified on hardware 2026-09-17 by capturing SimAppPro driving the panel in a live Hornet mission. All three indices were seen taking values across the 0-255 range (1, 12, 123, 211 on UFC1 index 0; 1, 12, 123, 178 on UFC1 index 1; 2, 25, 251 on HUD1 index 1), which is what makes them dimmers rather than indicators.
One USB interface at PID 0xbede, two parts, both answering a broadcast heartbeat. The UFC and the HUD control panel below it are one physical assembly but separate part ids.
NO DISCRETE INDICATORS. Every light on both panels is either a backlight or the segment display, so nothing here is a lamp in the sense the PTO2 uses the word.
UFC1 carries a 96-byte segment display driven by SET_LCDS rather than SET_LEDX. Its cell and glyph map is data/displays/ufc1.json.

SimAppPro drives LCDBacklight only from its own slider, never from DCS. INST_PNL_Backlight it drives from DCS only when the user has set that device to sync mode. Neither is a constraint on us; it just means a capture will not show them moving unless the sliders are.

THE DISPLAY LATCHES, verified on hardware 2026-09-17: a pattern written with SET_LCDS was still on the glass minutes later with the writing process exited and no handle open. It must be blanked on mission end and on shutdown exactly as the lamps are. Writing zeros to all 24 groups clears it.

SET_LCDS is not acknowledged. 24 frames drew 0 replies from the same read window that had just taken an immediate echo from a SET_LEDX write to this device, so a display write cannot be confirmed the way a lamp write can.

leds.name: Backlight
leds.label: Panel backlight
leds.note: Lights the ICP legends. Verified on hardware 2026-09-18: driven from the F-16's PRIMARY CONSOLES knob, the legends dimmed and brightened with it.

leds.name: Screen_Backlight
leds.label: DED backlight
leds.note: Lights the DED: bound like any lamp, but it lights only while a profile puts fields on the screen and is 0 when nothing is drawn there. Every default holds it at full. At 0 a correctly drawn page is invisible. Verified 2026-09-18 by capturing the SimAppPro slider: SET_LEDX index 1 took values from 0x00 to 0x70 as it moved, and the DED followed. While SimAppPro is streaming to the DED it raises this to about 60 if the user has it lower, and puts the user's value back when the stream stops (observed on the panel, not captured).

_notes: One USB interface at PID 0xbf06 answering as part 0xbf06. It declares 64-byte reports and a second output channel, 0xf0, for the screen.
The DED is a 200x64 pixel screen, not a segment display. Its map is data/displays/ded.json and its protocol is in docs/PROTOCOL.md under "Driving a pixel display".
THE SCREEN LATCHES, verified on hardware 2026-09-18: a page stays on the glass after the writing process exits. It must be blanked on mission end and on shutdown exactly as the lamps are.

A PAGE CHANGE FLASHES, observed 2026-09-18: the DED shows a brief full-bright flash between the old page and the new one. SimAppPro driving the same panel does exactly the same, so it is the device, not our writes, and there is nothing to fix.
The lamp indices are SimAppPro's (www/js/DeviceConfig.js, AllDevice[PIDByName.ICP]): Backlight 0, Screen_Backlight 1. Both verified on hardware 2026-09-18.

leds.name: INST_PNL_Backlight
leds.label: Panel backlight
leds.note: Lights the bezel legends. Verified 2026-09-18 by capturing the SimAppPro slider with the unit named C: SET_LEDX index 0 took every value from 0x00 to 0xff, and typed values 1, 13 and 137 went out as sent. The part and index do not change with the name.

_notes: One physical MFD, three possible identities. SimAppPro renames it L, C or R so a user with several keeps stable bindings, and each name is its own USB PID: C 0xbee0, L 0xbee1, R 0xbee2, all measured 2026-09-18. Same part 0xbe0d and same serial under every name, so this entry and CarrierAce_MFD_C and CarrierAce_MFD_R differ only in PID and name.

The name lives in config offset 0xd8: C 0, L 1, R 2, all captured. Writing it drops the device off USB and it re-enumerates about a second later under the new PID. We never write it; WRITE_CFG_DATA is forbidden.

"1 Split 3" mode (config offset 0xd0: 2 on, 0 off) keeps this PID and name but enumerates as three collections, col01 to col03, with the side switch choosing which one the buttons report on. Only col01 has an output report, so Device::open picks the collection that declares one. The switch is a button (input byte 5: 0x10 bottom, 0x20 middle, 0x40 top) and sends no config write, no re-enumeration and no lamp traffic, so there is still one backlight.

leds.name: INST_PNL_Backlight
leds.label: Panel backlight
leds.note: Lights the bezel legends. Verified 2026-09-18 by capturing the SimAppPro slider with the unit named C: SET_LEDX index 0 took every value from 0x00 to 0xff.

_notes: The same hardware as CarrierAce_MFD_L under its C name, PID 0xbee0. See that entry's notes for the rename and "1 Split 3" mode.

leds.label: Panel backlight
leds.note: Lights the bezel legends. Same lamp as under the C name, which is where the slider was captured; the part and index do not change with the name.

_notes: The same hardware as CarrierAce_MFD_L under its R name, PID 0xbee2. See that entry's notes for the rename and "1 Split 3" mode.

devices.product_name: WINCTRL Orion Combat Rudder Pedals Metal

leds.name: Backlight_L
leds.label: Left pedal light
leds.note: SimAppPro's "Backlight L" slider, the light on the left pedal sensor. The vendor table calls it Backlight1. Captured 2026-09-18 taking 1 and 11, and confirmed on hardware the same day: with 0, 1 and 2 at 0, index 0 = 255 lit the left light alone.

leds.name: Backlight_R
leds.label: Right pedal light
leds.note: SimAppPro's "Backlight R" slider, the light on the right pedal sensor. The vendor table calls it Backlight2. Captured 2026-09-18 taking 2, 22 and 222.

leds.name: Logo
leds.label: WinWing logo
leds.note: SimAppPro's third slider, which lights the logo. Index 3, not 2, and absent from the vendor table entirely. Captured 2026-09-18 taking 1, 10 and 101. Kept as a lamp so a profile can hold it in step with the pedal lights.

_notes: One USB interface at PID 0xbef0 answering as part 0xbef0. SimAppPro's name for it is R1.

The vendor table (www/js/DeviceConfig.js, AllDevice[PIDByName.R1]) lists Backlight1 0 and Backlight2 1 only. SimAppPro's own UI has a third slider, and the capture put it on index 3. A vendor table is a hypothesis, as the PTO2's FLAG already showed.

INDEX 2 IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. It is not a lamp and not a gate: a write to it goes through to both pedal lights, and whichever write came last wins. Measured on hardware 2026-09-18 with dcs-signal led: with 1 and 2 at 0, 1=255 lit the right light alone, so 2 does not gate; 2=255 lit both with 1 at 0, so it drives them directly; then 1=0 put the right light out with 2 still at 255, so nothing of it stays latched; and 2=0 put both out. Index 0 alone lights only the left light, so 2 is a hidden fourth control over 0 and 1 together. SimAppPro never writes it. A profile keeps the lights together with same_as instead, which leaves each one addressable. Owning it would let a sweep overwrite L and R depending on write order, so nothing here addresses it.

_notes: One physical MCDU, three possible identities. SimAppPro renames it CAPTAIN, CO-PILOT or OBSERVER, and each name is its own USB PID: CAPTAIN 0xbb36, CO-PILOT 0xbb3e, OBSERVER 0xbb3a, all measured 2026-09-18. Same part 0xbb32 and same serial under every name, so this entry, MCDU_CoPilot and MCDU_Observer differ only in PID and name. It declares 64-byte reports and the 0xf0 screen channel, like the ICP.

The name lives in config offset 0xcc, byte 1: CAPTAIN 0, OBSERVER 1, CO-PILOT 2, all captured 2026-09-18 (byte 0 is 01 each time). Before the first rename it read ff and the panel was CAPTAIN. Writing it drops the device off USB and it re-enumerates about three seconds later under the new PID. We never write it; WRITE_CFG_DATA is forbidden.
Every index captured from SimAppPro 2026-09-18. The nine indicators were switched on and off in index order and only ever took 1 or 0. Indices 3 to 7 were never written.

The screen is a 24x14 text grid on report 0xf2, drawn from a font the panel is sent (data/displays/mcdu.json). SimAppPro's own screen buttons send only self-tests, cmd 0x104 with values 13 to 20 (white, black, red, green, blue, lime, purple, the WinWing logo). See docs/PROTOCOL.md.

_persisted_brightness.comment: SimAppPro saves panel brightness to device flash. Each part has its own config offset, and the layout is one byte per dimmer, in index order on every panel but the rudder pedals, which store theirs in SimAppPro's slider order. Observed by watching WRITE_CFG_DATA while moving the sliders.

0xbf06.note: Screen_Backlight's byte seen tracking the slider, 2026-09-18. Backlight's slot follows the index-order rule; its byte has not been seen changing.

0xbe0d.note: CarrierAce MFD, every name. Seen 2026-09-18: 06 c8 00 00 89 ff ff ff about a second after the slider settled on 137.

0xbef0.note: Orion Combat Rudder Pedals. Slider order, not index order: byte 2 is Logo at index 3. Seen 2026-09-18 ending 06 e8 00 00 0b de 65 ff after L 11, R 222, logo 101.

0xbb32.note: MCDU Captain. Seen 2026-09-18 ending 06 d0 00 00 87 87 87 ff after all three at 135, each byte written as its slider was released.

_persisted_brightness.warning: We must never write these. WRITE_CFG_DATA is persistent and is on the forbidden list. Reading them with READ_CFG_DATA is safe and is how the daemon can warn when a user's stored brightness would make correctly driven output invisible. The UFC has two such traps, not one: a dark LCDBacklight hides the whole display.
